review.basis: Four source-normalized energy-use templates for existing biofuel roles, using shared Premise normalization and complete native FAME supply.
limitations: Complete native used-cooking-oil biodiesel at the fuelling station is the screening FAME supply. It differs from generic oil-crop biodiesel in feedstock, waste allocation, production, delivery, geography and vintage; impacts are not equivalent and differences remain unquantified.

Keep the existing shared FAME nominal properties: 38 MJ/kg, 0.0734 kg CO2/MJ and its biogenic accounting convention. These are not a newly measured LHV or exact elemental carbon balance for this native mixture. No efficiency, density, extra fuelling loss, upstream uptake or recovery credit is invented.

Use the existing representative diesel vehicle powertrain, service energy denominator and signed equipment exchanges through shared normalization. Non-CO2 exhaust retains that powertrain proxy; no whole-vehicle body, roads, lifetime or payload factor is added twice. The legacy product label heat denotes this existing per-MJ energy-use inventory, not an added useful-heat output.

Keep the existing shared FAME nominal properties: 38 MJ/kg, 0.0734 kg CO2/MJ and its biogenic accounting convention. The weight of the diesel tank is calculated based on the following formula:  17.159*ln(V_diesel)-54.98 taken from Wolff et al. (2020).
V_diesel is taken from  Vossloh Rail Vehicles (2012), being 5,000l.
It is assumed that a diesel tank for heavy-duty road vehicles is similar in structure and material composition as a diesel tank used in locomotives.
The lifetime of the tank is assumed to be the same as the whole locomotive (40 years).

exchanges.comment:
ecoinvent inventory for 1 unit (max. power output 100kW, 53kg). The power output at wheel is 4x 600kW, so 2,400kW (Vossloh Rail Vehicles, 2012). This equals 24 ecoinvent equivalents.
The motors lifetime is assumed to equal the lifetime of the locomotive (40 years). Exact information on motors, including their lifetime is not available as locomotivve motors are produced to fit the vehicle and its power requirement. ABB (2017) mentiones that electric motors were still in good condition at the time of overhaul/maintainance after 20 years and the locomotive was prepared to run another 20 years. Material and energy requirements for maintainace of the motor are not considered.

activities.comment: Produces consumption of 1 MJ of purchased energy. Representative powertrain carrier: diesel. energy-specific equipment; excludes chassis, body, roads and whole-vehicle maintenance. Source transport, freight train, diesel-electric [Europe without Switzerland]; 0.391702807508409 purchased MJ per ton kilometer. All retained exchanges divided by this energy; lifetime, occupancy/payload and replacement allocation are carried by source production links. Baseline source specifications: This dataset provides 1 ton-kilometer of freight rail transport in Europe without Switzerland using a diesel-electric locomotive configuration. Within this workbook, the transport rows are structured as comparative decarbonization scenarios across diesel-electric, catenary-electric, and hydrogen fuel-cell traction for regional rail freight. This activity should therefore be read as a scenario-specific transport service inventory rather than as a generic average freight-rail market dataset. Screening limitations: Complete native used-cooking-oil biodiesel at the fuelling station is the screening FAME supply. It differs from generic oil-crop biodiesel in feedstock, waste allocation, production, delivery, geography and vintage; impacts are not equivalent and differences remain unquantified. Keep the existing shared FAME nominal properties: 38 MJ/kg, 0.0734 kg CO2/MJ and its biogenic accounting convention. These are not a newly measured LHV or exact elemental carbon balance for this native mixture. No efficiency, density, extra fuelling loss, upstream uptake or recovery credit is invented. Use the existing representative diesel vehicle powertrain, service energy denominator and signed equipment exchanges through shared normalization. Non-CO2 exhaust retains that powertrain proxy; no whole-vehicle body, roads, lifetime or payload factor is added twice.
